title: Power Display lists multi monitors of same one

comment.body: Thanks for the supplied monitor reports and archive. They show differing Windows monitor instance identities while the current scan sees one DDC/CI display. To distinguish an endpoint change from duplicate discovery, please describe the connection path (direct, dock, KVM or adapter) and the first transition that adds an entry, if known: sleep/wake, reconnect, another port, or Win+P. If the trigger is still unknown, please say so and describe the normal connection path.

information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguish a changed Windows endpoint from duplicate discovery, and avoid conflating two identical physical displays
information_gaps.how_to_collect: State whether the monitor is directly connected or uses a dock/KVM/adapter, and whether sleep/wake, reconnect, port changes or Win+P first causes another record. The supplied ZIP and monitor reports do not need to be uploaded again.
information_gaps.information: The connection route and exact display transition that adds a record

initial_investigation: Read the report, all current comments, labels, assignees and linked-work timeline; checked for existing coverage before proposing work.
Inspected the supplied monitor reports, Power Display discovery log and persisted settings/state; did not copy per-device identifiers into public context.
Traced MonitorIdentity.FromDevicePath and MonitorSettingsRebuilder.Rebuild: device-path instance segments are retained, and disconnected recent/hidden entries can remain.
Read related issue 48977. Its similar model-duplication symptom does not establish that the same identity transition causes this report.
inferences: Device-path identity churn plus retained disconnected settings is a plausible explanation; identical model names alone cannot prove physical-device identity or justify merging records.
issue_context.summary: Power Display accumulates disabled records when the same reported monitor acquires different Windows device-path identities.

plan: Reproduce one connection/sleep transition using the supplied report as the comparison baseline and trace discovery-to-settings keys.
Only after proving an unambiguous physical match, migrate the previous settings to the replacement key; preserve distinct identical-model displays and port-specific intentional configurations.
Provide a deliberate removal path for stale disconnected records, and add identity/retention regression tests before changing automatic matching.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Windows publishes a new device-path instance for the same display, while the old entry remains retained and the new key starts with default settings.

confidence.rationale: Distinct stored path identities and a single current DDC/CI target fit this mechanism, but the transition and safe physical identity criterion are not established. This is a lightweight proposal, not an approved implementation design.

proposed_fixes.title: Reconcile changed monitor identities without losing settings
verification: One physical display retains its intended settings after the confirmed transition; two identical displays remain separate; stale-record removal cannot delete an active display.
